issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a class named Stock (and instruct students to use a final Stock field in SealSaloon), but the template repository provides an Inventory class that implements the stock functionality while Stock.java is empty. The solution implementation also uses Inventory (static Inventory stock) instead of Stock. This naming/type mismatch (Stock vs Inventory) is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students: they will look for a Stock class to use/modify as described in the specification but find an empty Stock.java and a functioning Inventory.java, preventing them from following the instructions without making a naming/type decision.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the repository consistent with the problem statement: either provide a fully implemented Stock class in the template (moving or renaming Inventory implementation into Stock) and update references to use Stock throughout, or update the problem statement/UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock. Concretely, rename Inventory.java to Stock.java (or copy its implementation into Stock.java) and adjust all code and documentation to use the Stock type so students find the expected class and can implement SealSaloon as described.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML refer to a class named 'Stock' (the shared stock of ingredients), but the template and reference solution implement and use a class named 'Inventory' for the exact same concept. Additionally, the template includes an empty Stock.java file. This mismatch (Stock vs Inventory) forces students to map the described concept to a differently named class in the starter code and solution, creating unnecessary confusion when locating/implementing the expected functionality.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier across all artifacts. Either rename the Inventory class (and file) in template and solution to Stock (and update references), or update the problem statement and UML to refer to Inventory instead of Stock. Also remove or implement the empty template Stock.java to avoid an extra source of confusion.
